newsitem.title: USA: US spot propane mixed in quiet late trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot propane mixed in quiet late trade.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were mixed in quiet late trade on Monday, still finding support in a snap of cold weather that has overshadowed Monday's bearish Iraqi news.
Cold temperatures throughout much of the U.S. has put the focus on propane, which has been in high demand for home heating fuel and for the last last of crop drying.
"Propane prices have been tied more to the weather than what has been going on on the Merc," said one Conway, Kansas trader.
Crude oil futures dropped about 50 cents following news Iraq had agreed to all conditions for implementing the oil-for-food deal.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane dipped down a half cent in thin talk to between 68.00 cents and 68.50 cents a gallon. Traders said activity was nearly dead.
In the Midwest, Conway, Kansas, hub spot propane edged up a half cent to 79.50/80.00 cents, with 80.00 cent parcels sold.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
